content.question: How does reinforcement learning differ from supervised learning?
options: Reinforcement learning requires a large labeled dataset, while supervised learning does not.
Reinforcement learning learns by trial-and-error guided by rewards and penalties through interaction with an environment, while supervised learning relies on labeled datasets.
Reinforcement learning predicts continuous values, while supervised learning predicts discrete classes.
Reinforcement learning discovers co-occurrence rules in transaction data, while supervised learning groups similar data points.
content.answer: Reinforcement learning learns by trial-and-error guided by rewards and penalties through interaction with an environment, while supervised learning relies on labeled datasets.
